author: Sohaila Ahmed

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
```

## Background

Six participants performed barbell lifts correctly and incorrectly in five
different ways. Using accelerometer data from the belt, forearm, arm, and
dumbbell, we predict the manner in which the exercise was performed — the
`classe` variable (A–E).

## Data Cleaning

The training set (19,622 rows × 160 columns) contained many columns that were
mostly missing, plus identifier and timestamp columns that carry no predictive
signal. I removed columns with more than 90% missing values, then dropped the
seven identifier/timestamp columns (`X`, `user_name`, the two raw timestamps,
`cvtd_timestamp`, `new_window`, `num_window`) by name. This left 52 numeric
sensor predictors plus the `classe` label.

```{r load-clean}
train_raw <- read.csv("data/pml-training.csv",
                      na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
test_raw  <- read.csv("data/pml-testing.csv",
                      na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))

keep_cols <- colSums(is.na(train_raw)) / nrow(train_raw) < 0.9
train_clean <- train_raw[, keep_cols]

drop_names <- c("X", "user_name", "raw_timestamp_part_1",
                "raw_timestamp_part_2", "cvtd_timestamp",
                "new_window", "num_window")
train_clean <- train_clean[, !names(train_clean) %in% drop_names]
train_clean$classe <- as.factor(train_clean$classe)

dim(train_clean)
```

## Model and Cross-Validation

I used a **random forest** classifier, which handles the many correlated
accelerometer features and non-linear interactions without manual tuning. For
validation I split the training data 70/30 into a training set and a holdout
validation set using `createDataPartition`, stratifying on `classe`.

```{r model}
set.seed(123)
inTrain   <- createDataPartition(train_clean$classe, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train_set <- train_clean[inTrain, ]
valid_set <- train_clean[-inTrain, ]

rf_model <- randomForest(classe ~ ., data = train_set, ntree = 100)

pred_valid <- predict(rf_model, valid_set)
cm <- confusionMatrix(pred_valid, valid_set$classe)
cm$overall["Accuracy"]
```

## Expected Out-of-Sample Error

Validation accuracy on the 30% holdout was `r round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4)`,
giving an expected out-of-sample error of roughly
`r round(1 - cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4)` (about 0.5%).

## Test Set Predictions

The 20 test cases were aligned to the model's 52 predictor columns (dropping
the `problem_id` identifier) and predicted:

```{r test-pred}
model_vars <- names(train_set)[names(train_set) != "classe"]
test_clean <- test_raw[, model_vars]

pred_test <- predict(rf_model, test_clean)
pred_test
```
